stories.headline: India’s crude basket price tops $120 a barrel amid West Asia war
stories.title: India’s crude basket price tops $120 a barrel amid West Asia war
stories.summary: Indian basket crude import price hits multi-year high as marine insurance, freight rates rise
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: India’s average crude oil import basket price rose by almost 4 per cent month-on-month (M-o-M) in October to surpass the $120 per barrel mark as the conflict in West Asia exacerbated geopolitical uncertainty and pushed up marine insurance premiums and freight rates.
The average crude oil price for Indian basket stood at $120.46 per barrel till October 26, against $116.77 per barrel in September and $90.19 a barrel in August 2026.
The current October monthly average price is the highest in 14 years since March 2012 ($123.61 per barrel).
The crude oil Indian basket price on October 26 stood at $123.72 a barrel.
Meanwhile, global crude oil prices are also on the higher side, rising by roughly 80 per cent in 2026.
On Tuesday evening, Brent was ruling at $114.6 a barrel.
The WTI and Murban grades were trading at $100.9 a barrel and $117.7, respectively.
Besides, the under-recoveries on LPG for the three PSU OMCs are around ₹62,000 crore.
The Q2 FY27 results of HPCL and BPCL also reflect pressure on marketing margins, which is partially offset by high refinery margins.
Indian Oil is scheduled to present its results on Friday.
Analysts and refiners pointed out that record high shipping freight rates and high marine insurance premiums are adding more volatility to high crude oil prices.
Coupled with a weak Rupee against the US dollar is further inflating the bill besides pushing up the current account deficit (CAD).

stories.headline: Cyclone ‘Arnab’: National SARAS mela in Vijayawada closed to public on October 28
stories.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’: National SARAS mela in Vijayawada closed to public on October 28
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The National SARAS Mela–2026 at Punnami Ghat in Vijayawada will remain temporarily closed to the public on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), as a precautionary measure to ensure the safety of visitors, Self-Help Group (SHG) members, artisans, stall operators, and other staff.

Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP) Additional Director D. John said that the decision has been taken in view of the rainfall alert issued by the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) for the city, due to the very severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal.
In view of the prevailing weather conditions and anticipated risks, the officials have decided to temporarily suspend public access to the mela on Wednesday.
The National SARAS Mela–2026 will reopen to the public on October 29 (Thursday) and continue until October 31 (Saturday), subject to prevailing weather conditions and safety considerations.
As of October 26, the mela recorded cumulative sales of ₹10.54 crore, with 4.81 lakh products sold by Self-Help Group (SHG) women entrepreneurs, according to data available with the officials.
The cultural programmes organised as part of the mela are turning out to be a major attraction for visitors.
The performances of artistes from Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, and Andhra Pradesh garnered a lot of applause.

stories.headline: 47,830 people evacuated as cyclone Arnab triggers heavy rain in Odisha
stories.title: 47,830 people evacuated as cyclone Arnab triggers heavy rain in Odisha
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Arnab intensified over the Bay of Bengal, prompting Odisha to evacuate 47,830 people from vulnerable areas.
Heavy rain and winds impacted southern districts, with shelters and relief funds allocated to ensure safety.
Authorities warned against spreading misinformation about the storm.

Heavy rain and strong winds hit several districts of southern Odisha on October 27, 2026, as very severe cyclonic storm Arnab intensified over the Bay of Bengal, prompting the state government to step up evacuation and emergency preparedness measures ahead of the cyclone’s expected landfall on October 28.
The Odisha government evacuated 47,830 people from vulnerable areas in eight districts and identified 466 cyclone and flood shelters to accommodate affected residents.

Of those evacuated, 11,090 were from Nabarangpur; 11,000 from Gajapati; 9,850 from Malkangiri; 6,500 from Ganjam; 5,000 from Koraput; 2,415 from Kalahandi; 1,675 from Nuapada; and 300 from Rayagada, the state’s Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Kumar Pujari said in a statement from Bhubaneswar on October 27.
The impact of the cyclone also brought heavy clouds, rainfall and squally winds to coastal districts, including Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Puri, Bhadrak, Khurda and Balasore.
The storm is likely to move towards west-northwest before turning northwest and crossing the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28.
The system is forecast to bring winds of 125-135 kmph, gusting up to 150 kmph.

In a press statement dated October 27, Manorama Mohanty, director of the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Bhubaneswar, said the cyclonic storm intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by midnight on October 26, further strengthening into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of October 27.
Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Patil has released Rs 19 crore to support relief and preparedness operations in the eight affected districts.
Ganjam received Rs 5 crore, while Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Gajapati, Nabarangpur, Kalahandi and Kandhamal were allocated Rs 2 crore each, as per Pujari.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab prompts cancellation of 21 flights
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amaravati: At least 21 flights were cancelled at Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam airports on Tuesday as a very severe cyclonic storm approached the Andhra Pradesh coast, officials said.
At Vijayawada airport, five flights were cancelled on Tuesday, including four operated by IndiGo and one by Air India Express, an airport official told PTI.
The cancellations affected services to destinations such as Chennai, Bengaluru, Visakhapatnam and Kadapa, the official said.
For Wednesday, IndiGo has cancelled all its 12 flights at Vijayawada airport, while Fly91 has also cancelled flights and Air India has cancelled its morning service to Delhi.
A total of 15 flights have been cancelled for Wednesday, the official said.
At Visakhapatnam airport, 16 flights were cancelled on Tuesday.
In its latest bulletin, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said Cyclone Arnab was over the Bay of Bengal, about 170 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, at 11.30 am.
It was likely to move west-northwestward until evening before crossing the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, by Wednesday forenoon.
The system was expected to make landfall with maximum sustained wind speeds of 125-135 kmph, gusting to 150 kmph, the IMD said.
Andhra Pradesh has been placed on high alert, with evacuations planned and precautionary measures underway to prevent loss of life and property, officials said.

stories.title: Stand Together, Stay Safe: AP Govt Appeals to People Ahead of Cyclone Arnab
stories.summary: The exact information on whether or not it will be an extremely severe cyclone would be available in about two hours, IMD officials said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The exact information on whether or not it will be an extremely severe cyclone would be available in about two hours, IMD officials said.
Cyclone Arnab, as of now, is unlikely to intensify further into an extremely severe cyclone.
The very severe cyclonic storm moved west-northwestwards at a speed of 20 kmph during the preceding six hours and was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 8.30 am on Tuesday.
Though the indications are that it may not be an extremely severe cyclone, the administration has been put on high alert and efforts to meet the challenges are being made to meet any eventuality.
The Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed the officials to ensure evacuations and take all precautionary measures to avoid loss of life and property.
Already, over 1300 pregnant women have been shifted to hospitals.
In Kakinada district's Pithapuram area, rising sea waves have reached coastal areas, hitting Uppada, Konapapet and Moolapet, causing concern among residents.
According to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), the cyclone's effects had begun to be felt, with heavy rainfall likely shortly in north coastal Andhra districts.
Srikakulam district was likely to witness heavy rainfall accompanied by strong winds, while strong winds had begun in coastal districts such as Visakhapatnam and Kakinada.

CM, who is monitoring the cyclone continuously, directed officials to shift people living in low-lying areas to safer locations, ensure essential supplies at relief camps and minimise cyclone-related damage, as Cyclone Arnab is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on October 28, with heavy rainfall expected in north coastal districts.

"The cyclone, which was earlier classified as a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal, has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm and is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, by the forenoon of October 28," the Met department said in an official press release.

The system was located 220 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 240 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 340 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam, 370 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha and 410 km east of Bapatla, the IMD said.

stories.headline: Keralam Assembly: Academic Election Commission for Keralam campuses under consideration, says Education Minister
stories.title: Keralam Assembly: Academic Election Commission for Keralam campuses under consideration, says Education Minister
stories.summary: Roji M. John said the government supported campus politics but was committed to curbing unhealthy practices while not infringing on students’ democratic right to protest
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The State government is considering setting up an ‘Academic Election Commission’ on campuses to introduce constructive reforms in student union elections, Higher Education Minister Roji M. John said in the Keralam Assembly on Tuesday.

Replying to a submission by Uma Thomas, the Minister said the government supported campus politics but was committed to curbing unhealthy practices while not infringing on students’ democratic right to protest.

Student politics had been active in Keralam’s colleges since the freedom struggle and it had evolved through the formation of various student organisations and campaigns to protect democratic rights, he pointed out.
Healthy political interactions helped students develop leadership skills, assimilate democratic and constitutional values, all the while contributing to a vibrant and active campus environment.
However, in at least some institutions, the government has taken note that campus politics was taking an unhealthy turn, he said.
The government’s policy has been to curb such practices without curtailing students’ right to democratic protest, the Minister said.

Apart from revising the college election processes, the government was also introducing the ‘Sidharthan Student Distress App’, announced in the Budget and included in the 100-day action programme and the ‘Sidharthan Anti-Ragging and Student Welfare Act’, aimed at safeguarding student welfare, as part of its intensive efforts to check unhealthy practices on campuses.
The government’s policy was to encourage campus politics, but any activities that disrupt the peace and harmony on campuses will not be allowed, Mr. John said.

stories.headline: Centre transfers 2 senior IAS officers from J&K to Delhi
stories.title: Centre transfers 2 senior IAS officers from J&K to Delhi
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 27: The Centre has transferred two senior IAS officers, Ashwani Kumar and Dr Ashish Chander Verma, from Jammu and Kashmir to the Delhi segment of the AGMUT cadre, amid the impending change at the top of the Union Territory’s bureaucracy. According to an order issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on October 27, Ashwani Kumar, a 1992-batch IAS officer, and Ashish Chander Verma, a 1994-batch officer, have been transferred with immediate effect. The transfers will remain in force until further orders. Both officers are senior in batch to Sajjan Singh Yadav, a 1995-batch IAS officer appointed as the next Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir. Yadav is scheduled to assume charge on November 1, succeeding Atal Dulloo, who retires on October 31.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Needs Proper Roster Ruling Out Manual Intervention Of CJI: Justice Oka
stories.title: Supreme Court Needs Proper Roster Ruling Out Manual Intervention Of CJI: Justice Oka
stories.summary: There is no proper roster in the Supreme Court if categories of cases can be assigned to multiple benches, the former judge says.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: There is no proper roster in the Supreme Court if categories of cases can be assigned to multiple benches, the former judge says.

Former Supreme Court Judge Justice Abhay S Oka has said that the Supreme Court needs to introduce a proper roster system that rules out the possibility of manual intervention by the Chief Justice of India in the allocation of cases to benches.

Speaking on the topic "Accountability of Judges" at a seminar organised by the Campaign for Judicial Accountability and Reforms in New Delhi, Justice Oka said that the absence of a proper roster in the Supreme Court raises questions about how cases are assigned to particular benches.
"The object of the roster is to rule out the possibility of manual intervention in listing.
If there is a roster, the Chief Justice of the High Court or the Supreme Court will not have any right to manually intervene in the listing of any particular case," he said.
Pointing out that the Supreme Court's roster assigns certain categories of cases to multiple benches, he said that lawyers are often left unaware of which bench will hear their cases.
"If you go to the Supreme Court, there is unfortunately no proper roster.
In the Supreme Court, you will find a caption, 'Judges' Roster'.
What does it contain?
Even the latest roster of October 26 only gives a subject-wise list.
There are categories numbered 301 to 306, and these categories are assigned to four different benches," he said.

For instance, a Special Leave Petition challenging a High Court order in an environmental matter could be assigned to any one of several benches, leaving the lawyer uncertain about which bench would hear the case.

stories.headline: Why Most Medicines Kept Out Of Price Control Regime? Supreme Court Questions Centre, Reserves Order
stories.title: Why Most Medicines Kept Out Of Price Control Regime? Supreme Court Questions Centre, Reserves Order
stories.summary: “What stops you from taking control of the entire range of medicines and drugs?” SC asked the Centre.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: “What stops you from taking control of the entire range of medicines and drugs?” SC asked the Centre.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday questioned why the Union government was reluctant to bring a wider range of medicines under price control, observing that its reliance on market forces and concerns about pharmaceutical-industry growth cannot justify leaving patients exposed to medicine prices that may be hundreds of times higher than procurement costs.
“You are dealing with the lives of people, Ms. Bhati.
Don't take it as a commerce.
Treat it as a life of the poorest person of this country.
You are talking only in the terms of commerce, economic policy, this, that.

Is this a matter in which economic policy will be supreme as compared to the life of the citizens at large?” Justice Sandeep Mehta asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, who was defending the Centre's pharmaceutical pricing policy.

The Court reserved its order in the case concerning regulation of medicine prices after questioning the Centre over the substantial difference between the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines and the prices at which retailers procure them.
The Court also questioned why a large proportion of medicines remained outside the stricter price-control regime under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013 (DPCO).

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta repeatedly asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati to explain why the government permitted manufacturers to print MRPs several times higher than the prices charged to dealers and retailers.

During the hearing, Justice Sandeep Mehta recounted an incident in which a medical dealer, whose wife was undergoing cancer treatment at a prominent hospital, wanted to procure a chemotherapy injection for her at the dealer price of ₹11,000.
The hospital refused to administer the injection and charged ₹1.3 lakh for it, he said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court questions Centre over huge gap between medicine MRP and retailer prices
stories.title: Supreme Court questions Centre over huge gap between medicine MRP and retailer prices
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday questioned the Centre over the wide gap between the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines and the price at which retailers purchase them, asking whether the government could justify what it described as “loot” and whether pharmaceutical manufacturers should be allowed to “run amok”.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta criticised the functioning of the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), describing it as seemingly “totally defunct”, and questioned why the drug pricing system appeared to favour manufacturers over patients.
The court reserved its verdict on two petitions concerning drug pricing, including pleas for stricter controls to ensure medicines remain affordable.
During the hearing, the Centre referred to its decision to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of their maximum retail price.
The Bench, however, questioned why a uniform trade margin of 16 per cent could not be introduced for all medicines.
“The government policy is that entire ecosystem is not to be controlled,” Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the Bench.
The judges pointed to a medicine with a price to retailer (PTR) of Rs 15 but an MRP of Rs 250, questioning the justification for such a substantial difference.
“Can you show any justification for this loot,” the Bench asked, adding that the government was allowing the practice to continue under its watch.
When Bhati referred to the need for regulatory control, the court asked, “Should it be allowed to run amok?”
The law officer argued that medicine prices in India were among the lowest in the world.
However, the Bench questioned why the pricing system appeared to work in favour of pharmaceutical manufacturers.
“Why is the entire system working to help these people (manufacturers),” the judges asked.
